title: Evaluating Regional Pulmonary Deposition using Patient-Specific 3D Printed Lung Models
protocol: Convert patient CT scans to 3D objects (.stl files).
Render CT scans into a 3D object using CT scan software.
Open the CT scan and create a mask on the airspace using the Threshold tool with a setting in the range of -800 to -1000.
View the 3D rendering and export the object as an .stl file using the 3D Preview tool.
Import the files into mesh editing software.
Remove any jagged features using the Select tool (Sculpt | Brushes: "Shrink/Smooth" | Properties: Strength (50), Size (10), Depth(0)).
Smooth the surface (Ctrl+A | Deform | Smooth | Smoothing (0.2), Smoothing Scale (1)).
Extend the wall of the objects by 2 mm in mesh editing software.
Slice the object at the trachea to form an inlet.
Create outlets at generations 2 or 3 where the object branches off to each lobe.
Modify patient lung model outlet geometries to be compatible with previously designed lobe outlet cap components.
Import the 3D object into 3D modeling software as a Solid Body.
Create a plane based on a face at each of the outlets.
Trace the inner wall and outer wall of the outlet in a sketch on the plane.
Import 3D part files into slicing software.
Choose hard resin for printing lung models and barbed tubing connections.
Choose soft resin for printing caps.
Set part orientation with lobe outlets facing away from the print platform.
View individual slices to check for “islands” and unvented volumes.
Add supports to any remaining “islands” and areas with significant overhangs.
Export and view slices to verify all areas are properly supported.
Print experimental components.
Complete post-processing as per manufacturer instructions.
Screw 1/4” barbed tube fittings into the side of the manifold with 6 ports and a 3/8” barbed tube fitting into the remaining port.
Cut 1/4" tubing to desired lengths and insert into each end of the push-to-connect valves.
Attach each valve to one of the 1/4" fittings inserted in the manifold.
Connect a flow meter to the other end of each valve.
Position the tubing system on top of the wooden board.
Add two screws to the side of the wooden board.
Attach the manifold to the screws using wire.
Add four screws around each of the valves and flow meters.
Use wire to secure each valve and flow meter to the wooden board.
Connect the manifold to an in-line 0.1 µm pore size vacuum grade filter with approximately 6” of 3/8” ID tubing.
Connect the other end of the filter to the flow controller using another 6” of 3/8” ID tubing.
Insert barbed tubing connection into the cap with nozzle protruding through the opening in the cap base.
Insert one end of the oval barbed tubing connection base into the cap.
Stretch the flexible cap over the other end of the oval base carefully.
Cut 10 μm filter paper such that it is slightly larger than the outlet area.
Fold the filter paper over the lobe outlet.
Hold the folded filter paper in place with one hand.
Use tweezers to stretch the cap with barbed tubing connection over the outlet.
Press the cap down until the cap’s notch matches up with the corresponding notch on the lobe outlet.
Repeat for all remaining lobe outlets.
Connect each lung model lobe outlet to the tubing of the corresponding flow meter and valve.
Attach the electronic flow meter to the lung model mouth inlet to measure total air flow rate to the lung model.
Turn on the flow controller.
Turn on the vacuum pump.
Select the “test setup” setting on the flow controller.
Slowly increase the flow rate until the electronic flow meter displays the desired total flow rate.
Adjust the flow rate through each of the five lung lobes using valves.
Set the flow rates for Right Upper (RU), Right Middle (RM), Right Lower (RL), Left Upper (LU), and Left Lower (LL) to steady values.
Check the overall flow rate again on the electronic flow meter.
Verify that there are no leaks in the system by ensuring consistent total flow rate.
If there is a discrepancy, lower the flow rate with the flow controller.
Set all valves to the fully open configuration.
Repeat steps 4.2 and 4.3 until the total flow rate is correct.
Leave the vacuum pump on once desired flow rates are set.
Perform experiments in a fume hood with the sash closed.
Fill nebulizer with solution of desired fluorescent particles.
Connect nebulizer to lung model inlet without targeting device for validation.
Connect nebulizer to targeting device and insert into lung model.
Connect compressed air line to nebulizer.
Set flow controller to run for one 10 s trial.
Open compressed air valve slightly before pressing start on the flow controller.
Press start on the flow controller and immediately open compressed air valve fully.
Begin to close compressed air valve once the flow controller reaches about 9 s.
Close the compressed air valve fully.
Disconnect the nebulizer from the compressed air line.
Fully close the fume hood sash.
Shut off the vacuum pump.
Wait for about 10 minutes to clear any aerosols from the fume hood.
Disconnect the lung model from the tubing system carefully.
Remove lobe outlet caps using tweezers by lifting them gently.
Take out the filter paper from each cap and place it into a 24 well plate with the particle-deposited side facing down.
Label each well corresponding to each lobe.
Place the well plate into the digital fluorescence microscope.
Set the microscope to 4x magnification.
Select the appropriate fluorescence channel.
Visually identify which lobe’s filter paper has the highest amount of particle deposition.
Use the “Auto Expose” function.
Note the resulting exposure and integration time values.
Apply this exposure setting to all filters for the run.
Assess whether the settings produce a satisfactory image for high deposition areas.
Change focus settings from filter to filter as necessary.
Ensure flatness of filter paper against the bottom of the well plate.
Take at least three images of each lobe’s filter paper at random locations.
Save images as .tiff files.
Import all filter paper pictures for a given run into an ImageJ session.
Change each image’s type to 8-bit by selecting Image | Type | 8-bit.
Open the picture with the highest fluorescence and select Image | Adjust | Threshold to open a threshold window.
Adjust the threshold values to minimize background signal from the filter paper and clearly define the edges of particles.
Propagate the threshold settings for the highest fluorescence image to all other images.
Quantify the number of particles by selecting Analyze | Analyze Particles.
Quantify the total fluorescent area by selecting Analyze | Analyze Particles.
